questions.questionText: A transaction is:
options: A single unit of work that either fully succeeds or fully fails
questions.correctAnswer: A single unit of work that either fully succeeds or fully fails
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: A single unit of work that either fully succeeds or fully fails.

questions.questionText: Which property ensures all operations in a transaction complete or none do?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Atomicity.

questions.questionText: Which ACID property ensures the database moves from one valid state to another?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Consistency.

questions.questionText: Which ACID property ensures concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Isolation.

questions.questionText: Which ACID property ensures committed changes survive system failures?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Durability.

questions.questionText: What does ACID stand for?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.

questions.questionText: In which transaction mode does SQL Server automatically start a new transaction after the previous one completes?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Implicit transactions.

questions.questionText: In which transaction mode is each individual statement committed automatically?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Autocommit.

questions.questionText: In explicit transactions, the user:
options: Defines the start and end with BEGIN TRANSACTION and COMMIT/ROLLBACK
questions.correctAnswer: Defines the start and end with BEGIN TRANSACTION and COMMIT/ROLLBACK
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Defines the start and end with BEGIN TRANSACTION and COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

questions.questionText: Batch-scoped transactions apply to:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Multiple Active Result Sets (MARS).

questions.questionText: Which statement starts an explicit transaction?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: BEGIN TRANSACTION.

questions.questionText: Which statement makes the changes of a transaction permanent?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: COMMIT TRANSACTION.

questions.questionText: Which statement undoes all changes made in a transaction?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION.

questions.questionText: Which statement creates a savepoint inside a transaction?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: SAVE TRANSACTION.

questions.questionText: Rolling back to a savepoint:
options: Undoes only the work after the savepoint
questions.correctAnswer: Undoes only the work after the savepoint
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Undoes only the work after the savepoint.

questions.questionText: Which function returns the number of active BEGIN TRANSACTION statements for the current connection?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: @@TRANCOUNT.

questions.questionText: When BEGIN TRANSACTION is executed, @@TRANCOUNT is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Incremented by 1.

questions.questionText: When COMMIT TRANSACTION is executed on the outermost transaction, @@TRANCOUNT becomes:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: 0.

questions.questionText: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION (without savepoint) sets @@TRANCOUNT to:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: 0.

questions.questionText: The WITH MARK option in BEGIN TRANSACTION:
options: Marks the transaction in the log
questions.correctAnswer: Marks the transaction in the log
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Marks the transaction in the log.

questions.questionText: Marked transactions are useful for:
options: Restoring related databases to a logically consistent point
questions.correctAnswer: Restoring related databases to a logically consistent point
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Restoring related databases to a logically consistent point.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of characters used from a transaction name?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: 32.

questions.questionText: A transaction name variable can be declared as:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: char, varchar, nchar, or nvarchar.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a concurrency problem?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Dirty read.

questions.questionText: A dirty read occurs when a transaction:
options: Reads data modified by another transaction that has not yet committed
questions.correctAnswer: Reads data modified by another transaction that has not yet committed
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Reads data modified by another transaction that has not yet committed.

questions.questionText: A nonrepeatable read occurs when:
options: A row read twice in a transaction returns different values
questions.correctAnswer: A row read twice in a transaction returns different values
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: A row read twice in a transaction returns different values.

questions.questionText: Phantom reads occur when:
options: New rows matching a query appear when it is re-run in the same transaction
questions.correctAnswer: New rows matching a query appear when it is re-run in the same transaction
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: New rows matching a query appear when it is re-run in the same transaction.

questions.questionText: A lost update occurs when:
options: Two transactions update the same row and one overwrites the other's change
questions.correctAnswer: Two transactions update the same row and one overwrites the other's change
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Two transactions update the same row and one overwrites the other's change.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level allows dirty reads?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: READ UNCOMMITTED.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level is the default in SQL Server?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: READ COMMITTED.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level prevents dirty reads but allows nonrepeatable reads?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: READ COMMITTED.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level prevents dirty reads and nonrepeatable reads but not phantoms?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: REPEATABLE READ.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level is the most restrictive and prevents phantoms?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: SERIALIZABLE.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level uses row versioning to give a transaction a consistent view of the data?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: SNAPSHOT.

questions.questionText: Which statement sets the isolation level for a session?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL.

questions.questionText: Locking is used by SQL Server to:
options: Control concurrent access and maintain data consistency
questions.correctAnswer: Control concurrent access and maintain data consistency
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Control concurrent access and maintain data consistency.

questions.questionText: A shared (S) lock is used for:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Read operations.

questions.questionText: An exclusive (X) lock is used for:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Data modification operations.

questions.questionText: An update (U) lock is used on resources that:
options: Can be updated, to prevent a common form of deadlock
questions.correctAnswer: Can be updated, to prevent a common form of deadlock
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Can be updated, to prevent a common form of deadlock.

questions.questionText: Intent locks are used to:
options: Indicate a lock will be placed at a lower level in the hierarchy
questions.correctAnswer: Indicate a lock will be placed at a lower level in the hierarchy
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Indicate a lock will be placed at a lower level in the hierarchy.

questions.questionText: Which lock is used while performing a table DDL operation such as adding a column?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Schema modification lock.

questions.questionText: Bulk update (BU) locks are used when:
options: Bulk copying data into a table with the TABLOCK hint
questions.correctAnswer: Bulk copying data into a table with the TABLOCK hint
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option B: Bulk copying data into a table with the TABLOCK hint.

questions.questionText: A shared lock and an exclusive lock on the same resource are:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Not compatible.

questions.questionText: A deadlock occurs when:
options: Two or more transactions block each other, each waiting for the other's lock
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more transactions block each other, each waiting for the other's lock
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Two or more transactions block each other, each waiting for the other's lock.

questions.questionText: SQL Server resolves a deadlock by:
options: Choosing a victim transaction and rolling it back
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing a victim transaction and rolling it back
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Choosing a victim transaction and rolling it back.

questions.questionText: By default, each individual SQL statement in SQL Server is:
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Transactional (autocommit).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is NOT allowed inside a transaction?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: CREATE DATABASE.

questions.questionText: The transaction log records:
options: All transactions and the database modifications made by each
questions.correctAnswer: All transactions and the database modifications made by each
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: All transactions and the database modifications made by each.

questions.questionText: Log truncation frees:
options: Space in the log for reuse
questions.correctAnswer: Space in the log for reuse
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option C: Space in the log for reuse.

questions.questionText: Which recovery model supports point-in-time recovery by keeping full log history?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: Full recovery model.

questions.questionText: Which recovery model automatically reclaims log space at checkpoints?
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option D: Simple recovery model.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about a transaction that is rolled back?
options: All its data modifications are undone
questions.correctAnswer: All its data modifications are undone
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: All its data modifications are undone.

questions.questionText: In a funds transfer, why is a transaction essential?
options: So debit and credit either both succeed or both fail
questions.correctAnswer: So debit and credit either both succeed or both fail
questions.explanation: Correct answer is option A: So debit and credit either both succeed or both fail.
